# Scrappling Agent Guide

> Use this file when an AI agent needs to scrape a public URL through Scrappling and return structured content.

Scrappling exposes a simple scraping API for public web pages. The easiest route for agents is the frontend proxy:

```text
POST /api/scrape
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com/article"
}
```

The response is always JSON. The API returns HTTP 200 for both success and handled errors; inspect the `ok` field.

## When to use Scrappling

Use Scrappling when you need:

- Clean visible text from a public page.
- Markdown converted from the fetched page.
- Page metadata such as title, status, links, and images.
- A single URL scrape from an agent workflow.

Do not use Scrappling for:

- Private pages, logged-in pages, or user data.
- Paywall, CAPTCHA, or access-control bypass.
- High-rate crawling without permission.
- Actions that violate a site's terms or robots policy.

## Quick examples

### cURL

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://YOUR_SCRAPPLING_HOST/api/scrape" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url":"https://example.com"}'
```

### JavaScript

```js
const response = await fetch("https://YOUR_SCRAPPLING_HOST/api/scrape", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ url: "https://example.com" }),
});

const result = await response.json();
if (result.ok) {
  console.log(result.markdown);
} else {
  console.error(result.code, result.message);
}
```

### Python

```python
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://YOUR_SCRAPPLING_HOST/api/scrape",
    json={"url": "https://example.com"},
    timeout=60,
)
result = response.json()

if result["ok"]:
    print(result["markdown"])
else:
    raise RuntimeError(f'{result["code"]}: {result["message"]}')
```

## Success response

```ts
type ScrapeSuccess = {
  ok: true;
  finalUrl: string;
  status: number;
  title: string | null;
  description: string | null;
  text: string;
  markdown: string;
  html: string;
  links: { href: string; text: string }[];
  images: { src: string; alt: string | null }[];
  fetchedAt: string;
  fetcher: "StealthyFetcher" | "PlayWrightFetcher" | "Fetcher" | "JinaReader";
};
```

Prefer `markdown` for agent context. Use `text` for compact summaries. Use `links` and `images` when you need page references or media candidates.

## Error response

```ts
type ScrapeError = {
  ok: false;
  code:
    | "INVALID_URL"
    | "PYTHON_MISSING"
    | "SCRAPLING_MISSING"
    | "TIMEOUT"
    | "FETCH_FAILED"
    | "PARSE_FAILED"
    | "UNKNOWN";
  message: string;
  detail?: string;
};
```

Retry only when `code` is `TIMEOUT`, `FETCH_FAILED`, or `UNKNOWN`. Do not retry aggressively.

## Behavior notes

- The frontend proxy normalizes URLs and calls the Scrapling backend.
- Production uses the deployed backend at `https://scrappling-b092deec.serverless.boltic.app` unless configured otherwise.
- The proxy currently requests the stealth fetcher and HTML return from the backend, then converts the HTML into JSON and Markdown.
- If the first result looks like a block page, the proxy can fall back to Jina Reader and return `fetcher: "JinaReader"`.
- The frontend proxy has an approximate 30 second hard timeout per fetch attempt.

## Raw backend API

If you are calling the backend directly, use:

```text
POST https://scrappling-b092deec.serverless.boltic.app/scrape
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "url": "https://quotes.toscrape.com/",
  "fetcher": "http",
  "css": [".quote .text::text", ".author::text"],
  "xpath": null,
  "return_html": false,
  "timeout": 30,
  "headless": true,
  "network_idle": false
}
```

Raw backend fetchers:

- `http`: Fast plain HTTP fetch.
- `stealth`: Browser-backed Scrapling fetcher.
- `dynamic`: Playwright Chromium fetcher.

The backend also exposes `GET /openapi.json` for machine-readable schema discovery.

## Recommended agent workflow

1. Fetch `/llms.txt` first.
2. Fetch `/llms-full.txt` if you need request and response details.
3. Call `POST /api/scrape` with one normalized public URL.
4. Read `result.ok`.
5. Use `result.markdown` as the primary scraped content.
6. Cite or store `result.finalUrl` and `result.fetchedAt` with downstream work.
